items.title: Aging Safely Baths Confirms Ella’s Bubbles Dealership, Putting Four Walk-In Tub Brands Under One BBB-Accredited Roof
items.summary: Aging Safely Baths is an Ella's Bubbles dealer, so families can compare Ella's Bubbles, Hydro Dimensions, Bestbath and Meditub tubs with one BBB-accredited company.
items.content_text: Aging Safely Baths has confirmed that it is a dealer for Ella's Bubbles walk-in tubs. With Ella's Bubbles in the lineup, the Denver-area company now offers four walk-in tub and accessible bathing brands: Hydro Dimensions, Ella's Bubbles, Bestbath (including the RANE by Bestbath line) and Meditub. A family can line up all four with one BBB-accredited company instead of booking a separate sales visit for each brand. The confirmation targets a familiar frustration. A household that wants to compare walk-in tubs often finds that each brand is sold by a different dealer, and every dealer recommends the brand it carries. That leaves the comparison to an adult child on a laptop or a parent with a stack of brochures. Carrying several brands lets one consultation answer the practical questions side by side: which door direction fits the room, how high the seat sits, how the tub will be heated and filled, and what the existing water heater can support. > Nobody should have to pick a brand before they know what fits the bathroom. items.title: Aging Safely Baths Publishes a Six-Point Fit Check for Families Shopping for a Walk-In Tub
items.summary: Six measurements to take before requesting a walk-in tub quote, from doorway width to water heater capacity, published by the accessible bathing supplier.
items.content_text: Aging Safely Baths, a walk-in tub and barrier-free shower supplier operating since 2012, has published a six-point fit check for families shopping for a walk-in tub. The check covers the measurements and household details that decide whether a model will work. The company says most quote requests stall because one of them comes up after a model has been chosen. The fit check is aimed at the adult children and spouses who usually do the research. In the company's experience, they often start from a product photo rather than the bathroom. > People fall in love with a tub online and then find out it won't go through the bathroom door. Ten minutes with a tape measure saves weeks. Measure first, then shop. Zach Wennstedt, founder of Aging Safely Baths. ## The six-point fit check **1. The alcove.** Measure the length, width and height of the space the current tub occupies. Many walk-in tubs are sized for a standard alcove, which can let the existing plumbing stay where it is. **2. The path in.** Measure every doorway and hallway turn between the front door and the bathroom. The tub has to travel that route in one piece. **3. items.title: Aging Safely Baths Explains Curbed vs. Barrier-Free Showers for Households Replacing a Bathtub
items.summary: When a low curb is enough and when a true zero-threshold shower is worth the floor work, from a Bestbath dealer that has installed both since 2012.
items.content_text: Aging Safely Baths, an authorized Bestbath dealer that has supplied accessible bathing products since 2012, has published guidance for households replacing a bathtub with a shower. The guidance covers the choice between a low-curb shower and a true barrier-free, zero-threshold shower. It explains what each requires underneath the floor and who each one suits. Replacing a tub with a shower is one of the most common accessibility projects in the home. The company says the decision is often made on looks, when the deciding factors are how the person bathing gets in and what the floor will allow. > A low curb is fine for someone who walks in steadily. A wheelchair or a rolling shower chair needs no curb at all, and that is a floor question before it is a product question. Find out what your floor will let you do, then pick the shower. Zach Wennstedt, founder of Aging Safely Baths. ## When a low curb works A curbed shower with a low threshold suits people who walk on their own or with a cane, especially with a grab bar at the entry.
